in_sanskrit.name: ईश्वर्या
in_sanskrit.meaning: Goddess of wealth, goddess of prosperity, goddess of all good things
in_sanskrit.long_meaning: ईशान (Ishana) + वर्य (varya) = ईश्वर्या (Ishwarya). Ishana, the god of the universe, is the source of all wealth, prosperity, and good things. Ishwarya is the goddess who embodies these qualities.

in_hindi.name: ईश्वर्या
in_hindi.long_meaning: ईशान (Ishana) के रूप की देवी। Ishana देवको सर्वशक्ति, सर्ववृद्धि, सर्वसुखकारी रूप के लिए पूजित जाती है। Ishwarya वह देवी है जो यह सारे शक्तियों और सुखदायक गुणों का रूप धारण करती है।

in_tamil.name: ஈஶ்வர்யா
in_tamil.long_meaning: ஈஶ்வர் (Ishvara) இல்லத்துவம் அவர்களின் இயலிப்பாக்கம். Ishvara, the supreme lord, is the source of all wealth and prosperity. Ishwarya is the manifestation of these qualities in the physical world.

in_telugu.name: ై౶్వర్౯ా
in_telugu.long_meaning: ై౶్వర్ (Ishvara) ఇద్దరిగా. Ishvara, the supreme lord, is the source of all wealth and prosperity. Ishwarya is the manifestation of these qualities in the physical world.

in_marathi.name: Ishwarya
in_marathi.meaning: हिंदू नाव म्हणजे Goddess of Wealth, Fortune
in_marathi.long_meaning: Ishwarya हे एक हिंदू नाव आहे जे भारतीय संस्कृतीत खोल आध्यात्मिक महत्त्व ठेवते। Ishwarya is the goddess of wealth, prosperity, and fortune in Hindu mythology. She is often depicted as holding a lotus or a pot of gold, and is believed to bless her devotees with material wealth and spiritual abundance. In Sanskrit, the name Ishwarya is derived from the words ishvara (God) and weya (giver), meaning 'Goddess who gives'.

in_bengali.name: Ishwarya
in_bengali.meaning: হিন্দু নাম যার অর্থ Goddess of Wealth, Fortune
in_bengali.long_meaning: Ishwarya একটি হিন্দু নাম যা ভারতীয় সংস্কৃতিতে গভীর আধ্যাত্মিক তাৎপর্য রাখে। Ishwarya is the goddess of wealth, prosperity, and fortune in Hindu mythology. She is often depicted as holding a lotus or a pot of gold, and is believed to bless her devotees with material wealth and spiritual abundance. In Sanskrit, the name Ishwarya is derived from the words ishvara (God) and weya (giver), meaning 'Goddess who gives'.
